lightPrompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one original OPDA editorial watercolour header illustration for a modelling documentation page.
Composition: a single coherent ultra-wide shallow 3:1 panorama, complete recognisable subjects and purposeful space, arranged side-to-side with no essential subject clipped. Not a grid, montage, screenshot, infographic or diagram. No surrounding frame.
Style: expressive refined architectural pen-and-ink drawing with soft pastel translucent watercolour and softly opaque gouache; organic varied contours, visible pigment variation, delicate hatching, clear silhouettes, warm humane professional magazine illustration.
Light palette: cool off-white #F9F9F9 paper to every edge, deep purple #231F2F ink, substantial softly coloured OPDA gold #FEC92B, petrol teal #0E8478 and violet #6C5BD4, with rose and coral; no beige or sepia cast.
Constraints: no text, lettering, digits, labels, handwriting, signatures, logos, wordmarks, watermark, private information, diagram arrows, abstract floating icons, puzzle pieces, handshake, checkmarks, badges, photography, 3D rendering, glossy objects, neon, glow or generic clipart. This is evocative editorial artwork, never formal notation or evidence. All papers and signs must be unlettered.
darkPrompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: dark-mode counterpart of an approved OPDA editorial watercolour header.
Input: the supplied light illustration is the exact EDIT TARGET.
Change only paper, ink value and pigment palette. Preserve every subject's identity, object count, positions, geometry, sizes, proportions, poses, viewpoint, perspective, framing, aspect ratio and negative space exactly.
Dark palette: flat deep-purple paper #131224 reaching every edge, visible between strokes; rich pastel gold, petrol teal, violet, rose and coral watercolour with softly opaque gouache; pale lavender and off-white fine linework wherever needed. Background must read purple, never brown, black or grey.
Constraints: no redesign, new objects, removals, different clothes, rearrangement, crop, night scene, stars, inversion filter, neon, glow, fluorescent outlines, text, letters, numbers, labels, signature or watermark. A palette edit only, not a new scene.

export.operation: Whole-image proportional resize; intrinsic source ratio retained without cropping or filters. Actual quality is recorded per asset.

pages.title: Make meaning a shared resource
pages.prompt: A long library display counter bearing one unfolding architectural paper scroll. At the left the scroll carries a small richly drawn British residential street study; its central portion unfurls into the detailed ink drawing of that same street, and at the right a slim transparent tracing sheet lifts above part of the drawing. A standing reader at one end and a seated architectural drafter at the other look at different parts without meeting around a table. Wide library windows and a very quiet low bookshelf behind. Show a shared subject examined through practical and formal views, with tactile paper and modest recognisable people. The scroll is an architectural sketch only, no writing or formal nodes.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of a reader and drafter examining an unfolding neighbourhood study and a transparent tracing layer in a library.

pages.title: Understand shared meaning
pages.prompt: A street-side conversation at the entrance of a modest British terraced home. A woman property practitioner with a petrol portfolio and an older man in a violet jacket examine the relationship between the main front door and a separate small side entrance, pointing gently to the actual doorway details rather than to a screen. Entire porch, low garden wall, gold door, coral brick and a little planted border extend in a shallow panorama. Human practical knowledge and an everyday question, no paperwork floating in the air, no cross-section, no table, no signs or house number.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of two practitioners examining a home's main and side entrances during an ordinary property discussion.

pages.title: Why shared meaning matters
pages.prompt: View from inside a quiet room across a broad window sill to one small cottage in the garden outside. On the sill are three separate tangible descriptions of that same cottage: a small folded perspective sketch, an unlettered open report with a simple cottage drawing, and a transparent plan sheet held in a low stand. The real cottage is visually distinct from the three accounts; the window frame and sill connect one calm wide scene. Petrol window trim, gold cottage door, violet notebook cover and coral flower pot. No people, text, numbers or diagram connectors.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of one cottage seen through a window, with a sketch, report and transparent plan on the sill as distinct descriptions.

pages.title: What we are building
pages.prompt: An elegant low archive cabinet in an architectural reading room, with six different shallow open drawers arrayed horizontally at varied modest depths. Their contents are complementary tangible specimens: blank definition cards, a single illustrated property sheet, branching paper topic dividers, a set of separate coloured choice swatches, one miniature doorway specimen and a small joined timber connection detail. Keep these tactile objects separate and useful, not six diagrams or floating icons. Cabinet violet with petrol and gold drawer interiors, rose and coral paper edges, organic detailed ink. No people or text; no copied index-card-box composition.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of six open archive drawers containing different paper and architectural specimens, suggesting complementary views of one agreement.

pages.title: Benefits, limits and reasonable objections
pages.prompt: An open architectural model carrying case rests on a broad bench, seen at low three-quarter angle. A carefully protected small dwelling model sits in petrol lining, its gold main room and separate coral enclosed-room piece clearly fitted but not merged. The removable enclosed piece rests partly outside the case, beside a simple unlettered scope sketch held by a violet clip. The empty fitted recess remains visible. Convey that making distinctions portable is useful but requires care and boundaries, not an automatic guarantee. The case lid and hinge create a strong horizontal silhouette. No people, seals, checkmarks, arrows, labels or puzzle imagery.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of a protected architectural model in an open carrying case, with a separate room piece and its visible fitted recess.

pages.title: Harbour Court: follow a question through the model
pages.prompt: A fictional compact two-storey British residential building opened at the front like an architectural cutaway, showing exactly two separate flats stacked one above the other. In the lower dwelling, one modest inspector stands in a living room beside an unmistakably closed coral door to a small glazed enclosed area; the upper dwelling remains separate and unoccupied. Two differently coloured unlettered report folders rest on a low plinth outside the building, distinct from the visit and the building. Petrol roof, pale gold rooms, violet architectural ink and coral details. Shallow wide full-building composition, no house name, numbers, text or precise dimensions.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of a two-storey residential cutaway with an inspector beside a closed door to a glazed area and separate report folders outside.

pages.title: How the modelling work is done
pages.prompt: A bright review studio with a long low wall-mounted pinboard of unlettered architectural extracts, varied paper edge tabs and one small dwelling sketch. At the left a standing domain practitioner pins a carefully selected source sketch; at the right a seated facilitator compares that source with a separate draft on a narrow drafting ledge, pencil poised. Papers have generous blank space, no printed words. An unused revision sheet lies underneath, indicating unfinished deliberation rather than approval. Distinct from a meeting table: wall, ledge, source and drafter form a shallow lateral scene. Petrol board, gold pins, violet and coral clothing.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of a practitioner selecting a source sketch while a facilitator compares it with a separate draft at a wall-mounted review board.

pages.title: Explore the model
pages.prompt: A close low horizontal view of a property-study display with one modest row-house maquette, its door, roof and adjoining garden wall clearly distinguishable. Three independent physical inspection lenses stand on small brass supports at different positions across the foreground, each revealing a different architectural detail: doorway, roof junction and boundary corner. Avoid optical distortion; these are real lenses beside one shared subject, not a formal diagram. Include a folded unlettered observation sheet at one end. Petrol and coral building washes, gold supports, violet shadows on cool white paper. No people, arrows, symbols, text or labels.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of three inspection lenses examining different architectural details of one residential model.

pages.title: Things, identities and relationships
pages.prompt: A straight-on eye-level street panorama of a single British townhouse facade with two clearly separate dwelling entrance doors, one petrol and one coral, within the same pale gold masonry frontage. A low unlettered address plaque is visibly attached to the building without becoming part of either door. At the far side, on a small outdoor ledge, a separate violet legal-document folder and a drawn building portrait are distinct physical objects. Show whole and parts and their descriptions remaining distinct, not a dollhouse cross-section or diagram. Include delicate railings and a small shrub, no people, words, digits or title seals.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of one townhouse facade with two separate dwelling entrances and a physically separate document folder and building portrait.

pages.title: People, roles and change
pages.prompt: A humane editorial street scene with one central adult seated on a low garden wall, holding two separate modest keyrings, one petrol and one coral. Two different residential entrances occupy the ends of the panorama, one gold Victorian doorway and one violet modern porch; a different counterpart person stands naturally near each entrance. The central person is shown exactly once, recognised as the same individual related to two distinct property settings. Natural body language, no handshake, no duplicate selves, no transaction papers, no badges, no labels, no numerals. Colourful pastel clothes, unlettered quiet street.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of one person holding two keyrings between two different residential entrances and their respective participants.

pages.title: Measurements, amounts and values
pages.prompt: Wide low interior perspective across a home's open living room and a visibly separate small glazed enclosure beyond its threshold. A surveyor kneels at the far left extending a plain unnumbered measuring tape across the main room; the enclosure has a coral floor wash distinct from the petrol main floor and a clear physical threshold. A folded blank measuring sheet and a violet pencil rest near the surveyor. The image highlights the inclusion boundary rather than exact arithmetic. Gold window light without dramatic glow, fine ink room details, no diagrams, numbers, currency, text, floating tools or labels.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of a surveyor measuring a main living room beside a clearly separate glazed enclosure and threshold.

pages.title: Dates, periods and applicability
pages.prompt: A long concertina-folded strip of blank calendar squares curves gently across a quiet broad shelf, each segment unnumbered. Separate tangible objects stand beside different parts without arrows: an inspector's folded field bag at one end, a closed violet report booklet in the middle, and a petrol record ledger near the other end. A translucent coral ribbon lies along only one short part of the strip to suggest a bounded period, not a mandatory workflow. No clock faces, hourglasses, miniature house or repeated previous desk composition. Gold clips, clean purple ink and soft pastel paper texture. No letters, numbers or status badges.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of an unnumbered concertina calendar beside an inspection bag, report and record ledger, with a ribbon marking only a bounded interval.

pages.title: Claims, evidence and uncertainty
pages.prompt: An observant interior vignette at a partly open threshold. In the foreground a bound sketchbook on a small stool contains an unlettered architectural drawing of the visible doorway. Beyond, one well-lit room can be seen, while a separate closed door conceals the adjoining area, making the limit of observation physically clear. A small mechanical inspection torch rests on the stool switched off; no beam or glow. The closed door is coral, visible room petrol, notebook violet and stool gold. No people, magnifying glass, source-document stack, hidden defects, padlocks, symbols, lettering or numbers.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of an observed doorway recorded in a sketchbook, while a separate closed door keeps an adjoining room out of view.

pages.title: Names, choices and classification
pages.prompt: An architectural sample room with a long freestanding display rail holding five distinct illustrated dwelling specimen cards by small gold clips. Each card shows a different dwelling silhouette, while several detached completely blank label strips lie below on a narrow ledge, separate from the depicted things. Small petrol, rose and violet paper tabs attach along independent edges rather than one nested tree. This is a tactile editorial arrangement about concepts, labels and facets, not an actual vocabulary or menu. No drawers, index boxes, people, text, letters, codes, symbols, arrows or numbers.
pages.alt: Pastel drawing of dwelling specimen cards on a display rail, with separate blank label strips and independently coloured classification tabs.
